question: How do errors in a learned causal graph turn into errors in the decisions it is used for, and at what accuracy (or with what guarantees) does a causal-discovery tool become worth using? Does moving directed-edge F1 from 0.63 toward the 0.957 identifiability limit matter downstream, or do reliability, calibrated confidence and abstention matter more?

schema.graph_metric: graph-level quantity (SHD, F1, SID input, expert accuracy, graph source)
schema.downstream_metric: decision-level quantity (SID/AID, interventional distance, ATE, regret, top-k RCA accuracy, validation hit rate)
schema.relation_found: what the source reports, quantified where reported
schema.threshold_or_target: explicit threshold or target stated by the source; null if none
schema.population: synthetic / semi-synthetic / testbed / real / theory / review
schema.label: reported (authors' own page, read 2026-10-12) / second-hand (from an earlier project note, not re-opened) / measured (ours, from project files)
schema.read_on: date the source was read (or the prior note's date for second-hand rows)

rows.setting: DAG estimates of a known DAG (illustrative example)
rows.downstream_metric: SID (pairs with wrongly inferred p(x_j|do(x_i)) under parent adjustment)
rows.relation_found: Two estimates with equal SHD to the truth differ in SID (one adds an edge, harmless for interventions; one reverses an edge).
rows.label: reported

rows.relation_found: SID(G,H)=0 iff G is a subgraph of H: extra edges cost nothing for intervention prediction.
rows.label: reported

rows.relation_found: PC best on SHD and worst on SID (authors' statement).
rows.label: reported

rows.relation_found: A random graph scored below PC's SID upper bound in 77 of 100 experiments.
rows.label: reported

rows.setting: 300 pairs of 30-node graphs differing by one edge
rows.relation_found: Mean mis-identified pairs 2.0 (ancestor), 5.9 (O-set), 11.2 (parent) for a single-edge difference.
rows.label: reported

rows.relation_found: Fully connected guess vs empty truth: SHD maximal, AID 0. Correlations between AIDs 0.09-0.73; authors: choice of distance is practically important.
rows.label: reported

rows.relation_found: Ancestor-AID is zero iff the guess respects the true causal orders. gadjid runs in ms at p=1000 vs hours for SID.
rows.label: reported

rows.relation_found: Mean FID: reversal 0.336, add/del directed 0.138/0.130, bidirected edits ~0.15-0.23; FID-SHD Pearson r=0.82 with wide spread within SHD bins.
rows.label: reported

rows.setting: Software systems (Postgres etc.) plus synthetic BNs
rows.downstream_metric: Total variation distance of interventional distributions
rows.relation_found: SHD-SID strongly correlated; SHD-TVD only very weakly (qualitative). Algorithm orderings differ between synthetic and empirical data. 6/91 papers used empirical data with interventional measures.
rows.threshold_or_target: Recommend interventional measures on empirical data
rows.label: reported

rows.graph_metric: structural metrics (86% sim / 54% real use only these)
rows.relation_found: Interventional metrics in 9.1% (sim) / 7.5% (real) of studies; unused 89% of the time when real data contain interventions; Sachs plateau SHD ~12; practitioners use discovery as exploratory tool.
rows.threshold_or_target: Recommend interventional metrics on unseen interventions
rows.label: reported

rows.relation_found: Many metrics fail to correlate strongly with posterior approximation quality, especially at small n.
rows.label: reported

rows.setting: Risk estimation from interventional data, p in {25..200}
rows.downstream_metric: causal risk = Jaccard distance of descendant sets, estimated with two-sample tests on interventional data
rows.relation_found: Estimated risk differences between methods usually have the correct sign ('large majority'); needs interventions on some nodes.
rows.label: reported

rows.downstream_metric: validity of adjustment sets for all pairs
rows.relation_found: D_top=0 iff the order gives a valid adjustment set for every treatment-outcome pair (Prop. 3.3); predecessors in a topological order are a valid set (Prop. 3.2).
rows.label: reported

rows.setting: Real game telemetry (77,698 users; n=1,170 analytic)
rows.graph_metric: SHD vs a domain-admissible baseline graph
rows.relation_found: PC (SHD 15) and BOSS (SHD 33) converge to ATE ~0.144; CFCI lowest SHD (11) but identifiable in one configuration only.
rows.threshold_or_target: Trust rule: CI excludes 0 and ATE defined
rows.label: reported

rows.relation_found: Bound coverage 0.93-0.99 (synthetic); IHDP bounds [2.4, 7.2] around true 4.7; PC-derived edge sets may exclude the truth.
rows.reference: Padh, Li, Casolo, Kilbertus, arXiv 2502.17030 (PMLR v275)
rows.label: reported

rows.setting: CausalArena semantic scenario, 25 vars, PC CPDAG
rows.graph_metric: skeleton recall (0.52 for PC on semantic)
rows.relation_found: True parent set of X among IDA candidates for only 7/25 variables; 52% of pairs single-valued within PC's class; 600 pairs in 0.06 s.
rows.label: measured (ours)

rows.setting: Causal Bayesian optimisation, unknown graph (ER 10-100 nodes, DREAM E. coli)
rows.relation_found: Only target's parents matter under their assumptions; CBO-U converges to true-graph optimum; CBO with wrong graph worse on average (no numeric regret in text read).
rows.label: reported

rows.setting: Causal bandits, unknown graph, causal sufficiency
rows.relation_found: Learning the parent set is suboptimal and can conflict with regret minimisation; near-optimal algorithms skip graph recovery.
rows.label: reported

rows.graph_metric: partial structure (ancestors of reward + some confounders)
rows.relation_found: Recovering the induced subgraph on An(Y) and a characterised confounder set suffices; full discovery unnecessary.
rows.label: reported

rows.setting: Microservice RCA (Online Boutique, Sock Shop, Train Ticket; CIRCA/RCD/CausIL synthetic)
rows.relation_found: PC/FCI/Granger/LiNGAM-based RCA 'similar to Dummy'; non-causal BARO Avg@5 0.94 (OB CPU) / 0.81 (TT CPU); CausalRCA 0.97 / 0.53 but 0.05 on CIRCA10; no correlation analysis reported.
rows.label: reported

rows.relation_found: Text: CIRCA and RCD best (Avg@5 0.46, 0.54); Table 6: BARO ~0.80, TraceRCA 0.77. Text/table inconsistent; re-read before citing.
rows.reference: Pham et al., RCAEval, WWW 2025, arXiv 2412.17015
rows.label: reported

rows.graph_metric: service map given vs no graph
rows.relation_found: Methods with the service map usually better (CIRCA top-3 0.86-1.00 in 4/6 settings); without a graph none beat ranked correlation; correlation best at top-1.
rows.label: reported

rows.relation_found: CIRCA + structural graph AC@5 0.763 (Avg@5 0.603) vs random-walk + PCTS AC@5 0.449 (Avg@5 0.290), ~40x slower; graph effect not isolated from scorer.
rows.reference: Li et al., CIRCA, KDD 2022, arXiv 2206.05871
rows.label: reported

rows.relation_found: RCD ~98% top-1 synthetic; Sock-shop top-1 0.11-0.71, sometimes below epsilon-Diagnosis; Psi-PC matches on synthetic but >150 min at 500 nodes vs ~22 s.
rows.label: reported

rows.relation_found: 78% top-1, 95% top-3 on labelled production incidents; users rated it helpful.
rows.label: reported

rows.setting: Deployed RCA, AWS cloud network, 35 labelled incidents
rows.graph_metric: Granger-learned event graph (cycles, some edges contradict domain knowledge)
rows.relation_found: Recall@3 85.7%, exact 74.3% vs rule baseline 62.8% / 48.6%; graph quality not analysed against RCA accuracy.
rows.label: reported

rows.setting: Yeast, 5,361 genes, 63 observational profiles vs 234 knockouts
rows.downstream_metric: precision of top-q predicted effects in true top 10%
rows.relation_found: Top 50: IDA 33 (66%), Lasso 10, elastic net 8, random 5 +- 2.1. DREAM4 10-gene: IDA 4,4,5,1,2 TPs at q=10 vs Lasso 1,1,0,1,2.
rows.reference: Maathuis, Colombo, Kalisch, Bühlmann, Nature Methods 2010
rows.label: reported

rows.setting: Yeast, 6,170 genes, 160 obs + 1,479 deletions, held-out blocks
rows.downstream_metric: strong intervention effects (SIE) in held-out deletions
rows.relation_found: Top 4 edges all SIEs; 7 of top 20 vs 0.03 expected by random.
rows.label: reported

rows.downstream_metric: mutant validation; yeast ROC vs plain IDA
rows.relation_found: 4 of 9 testable top-ranked mutants showed an effect (p<0.05, unadjusted); clear improvement over plain IDA on yeast (plot only).
rows.label: reported

rows.setting: DREAM5 E. coli / S. aureus community networks
rows.relation_found: 23 of 53 tested novel E. coli interactions supported (43%).
rows.label: reported

rows.setting: Single-cell GRN inference on curated Boolean models
rows.relation_found: Many algorithms near random early precision on at least one curated model; prior reports on experimental data near random.
rows.reference: Pratapa et al. (BEELINE), bioRxiv 642926 preprint (Nature Methods 2020)
rows.label: reported

rows.downstream_metric: mean Wasserstein of predicted edges; false omission rate
rows.relation_found: Interventional methods no better than observational; GRNBoost and sortnregress top; methods at precision-recall extremes (NOTEARS-linear 0.88 / ~0).
rows.label: reported

rows.relation_found: FGES 0.44/0.60 -> 0.71/0.68 with trivial knowledge; single wrong CI test created false collider that propagated (FCI).
rows.threshold_or_target: Use longitudinal data and maximal prior knowledge
rows.reference: Shen, Ma, Vemuri, Simon, Sci. Rep. 2020
rows.label: reported

rows.graph_metric: agreement with author-built common-knowledge graph (37 edges)
rows.downstream_metric: predictive and interventional inference (results not read)
rows.relation_found: Knowledge graph is observational, not interventional, per authors; results section not reached.
rows.label: reported

rows.relation_found: No article tested its DAG against data; 73% reported estimates from other or unclear adjustment sets.
rows.label: reported

rows.relation_found: ~60% use causal graphs; ~20% of users build them systematically; ~half know omitting an arrow is the stronger assumption.
rows.label: reported

rows.relation_found: Beats purely data-driven learning once new-edge orientation is right in at least 2 of 3 cases.
rows.label: reported

rows.setting: Active knowledge requests in Tabu, 16 networks, limit 0.5n queries
rows.label: reported

rows.setting: Lay STEM annotators (15) on 4-8 node BNLearn graphs
rows.relation_found: Triplet prompting: SHD 1.67-11.33, D_top mostly 0; pairwise produced cycles on two graphs.
rows.label: reported

rows.relation_found: Reliability on finite real data uncertain; need gold-standard datasets, mixed-type methods, communication guidelines; many scientists doubt causal analysis.
rows.label: reported

rows.relation_found: No downstream yield or cost measured; experts found results promising.
rows.label: reported

rows.relation_found: Task accuracy high despite low edge F1.
rows.reference: Yang et al., arXiv 2605.26029 (via cluster9 note)
rows.label: second-hand

rows.setting: LLM + data fusion, 26 networks, obfuscated names
rows.graph_metric: LLM orientation accuracy vs edge recall
rows.relation_found: LLM orientation 96% but edge recall 60.3%; fusion F1 0.760 vs data 0.662 vs LLM 0.572.
rows.label: second-hand

rows.setting: LLM as epsilon-expert orienting MEC edges
rows.relation_found: Guarantee broke in the authors' own LLM test (ALARM excluded truth even at small eta; overconfident LLM).
rows.reference: Long et al., arXiv 2307.02390 (via cluster4 note)
rows.label: second-hand

rows.setting: LLM pairwise direct-edge judgements, 12 models, 6 graphs
rows.relation_found: Verbalised ECE ~0.21, AUROC 0.448; cross-prompt agreement ECE 0.016, AUROC 0.772; >80% of reversed/indirect false positives at confidence 80-100.
rows.reference: Kumar et al., arXiv 2608.23660 (via cluster4 note)
rows.label: second-hand

proposals.DV-1: Held-out interventional claim accuracy with risk-coverage: label (t,y) up/down/none from CausalArena obs+int rows (3-7 targets per scenario, 28-67 rows each; resampling interventions) or Causal Chambers lt_interventions_standard_v1 via Mann-Whitney + BH; method claims from obs rows + output graph (descendant/sign via IDA/MPDAG or abstain); report precision of committed claims, coverage, AURC, precision at 50%/80% coverage; ceiling = true graph + obs rows; all on column-shuffled inputs.
proposals.DV-2: Target-choice regret (pick the released target with largest predicted effect on y, regret vs best observed shift, abstain at cost c) and experiment lift (precision@q of top-q ranked (t,y) claims / base rate).
proposals.companion: ancestor-AID and O-set-AID via gadjid next to F1, on shuffled inputs.
